==Problem==
In an All-Area track meet, <math>216</math> sprinters enter a <math>100-</math>meter dash competition. The track has <math>6</math> lanes, so only <math>6</math> sprinters can compete at a time. At the end of each race, the five non-winners are eliminated, and the winner will compete again in a later race. How many races are needed to determine the champion sprinter?

<math>\textbf{(A)}\mbox{ }36\qquad\textbf{(B)}\mbox{ }42\qquad\textbf{(C)}\mbox{ }43\qquad\textbf{(D)}\mbox{ }60\qquad\textbf{(E)}\mbox{ }72</math>

==Solutions==
===Solution 1===
From any <imath>n-</imath>th race, only <imath>\frac{1}{6}</imath> will continue on. Since we wish to find the total number of races, a column representing the races over time is ideal.
Starting with the first race:
<cmath>\frac{216}{6}=36</cmath>
<cmath>\frac{36}{6}=6</cmath>
<cmath>\frac{6}{6}=1</cmath>
Adding all of the numbers in the second column yields <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ 43}</imath>

===Solution 2===
Every race eliminates <imath>5</imath> players. The winner is decided when there is only <imath>1</imath> runner left. You can construct the equation: <imath>216</imath> - <imath>5x</imath> = <imath>1</imath>. Thus, <imath>215</imath> players have to be eliminated. Therefore, we need <imath>\frac{215}{5}</imath> games to decide the winner, or <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ 43}</imath>
